notes: Each run works on a fresh copy of evals/fixtures/android-catalog-fixture (an Android app on AGP 9.2.1 + Gradle 9.6.1 with built-in Kotlin; see its README for what each catalog entry exercises). Before a run: copy the fixture to a temp dir, add local.properties with sdk.dir, adjust org.gradle.java.home in gradle.properties if needed, and `git init` + commit on `main` so that 'nothing changed' can be checked. Replace <FIXTURE> with the copy's path. The prompts ask for the proposal only (stop at the gate). Version numbers drift as libraries publish new releases, so assertions are phrased by behaviour rather than exact versions.

evals.prompt: Review the dependencies of my Android project at <FIXTURE> and show me what's outdated, grouped by risk. Don't change anything yet — I just want the proposal.
evals.expected_output: Detection without editing the build (init script) or via the planner's metadata mode, then a risk-grouped proposal produced from scripts/plan.py and reviewed by the agent; stops at the gate.
assertions: Detected updates with the ben-manes plugin injected by the init script (no edit to build.gradle.kts) or with plan.py --source metadata, not by inventing versions.
Ran scripts/plan.py (passing --kotlin with the effective version from buildEnvironment, or noting why not).

Flagged the latest androidx core-ktx and the latest Compose BOM as needing compileSdk 37 (project: 36) — coupled, not safe — and offered the highest compatible versions as alternatives, making clear which of the two rows 'the safe ones' would apply.
Listed AGP and the Gradle wrapper as separate items that need their own explicit confirmation.
Flagged the old-scheme KSP (2.2.10-2.0.2) as a prerequisite to migrate before any Kotlin bump.
Noted that under AGP 9 built-in Kotlin the catalog's kotlin ref doesn't control the compiler (or kept Kotlin as an own-confirmation item blocked by KSP).
Put the JitPack entry android-pdfview under 'needs a decision' (unused / version not published), not as a bump.
Did not present AGP-internal tooling (com.android.tools.utp, lint-gradle) or Kotlin toolchain artifacts as catalog updates.
Stopped at the gate: no tracked file changed (git status clean apart from ignored/removed build outputs).
User-facing response is in English.

evals.prompt: Check the deps of <FIXTURE> without running Gradle — the build is slow on my machine. Is anything worth updating? There's a JitPack library in there too, don't skip it.
evals.expected_output: Uses the planner in metadata mode (no Gradle detection run), checks the JitPack entry through JitPack metadata, and presents a tiered proposal; stops at the gate.
assertions: Did not run the Gradle detection task; used scripts/plan.py --source metadata (or equivalent metadata lookups).
Checked com.github.barteksc:AndroidPdfViewer against JitPack metadata and reported that the catalog version isn't a published stable release (needs a decision).
Kept AGP, Kotlin and the Gradle wrapper out of the safe group.
Reported the unused entries (android-pdfview; KSP only declared with apply false) as decisions, qualified as coming from a static scan of the build files rather than a report.
Stopped at the gate: no tracked file changed.
User-facing response is in English.

evals.prompt: Revisa las dependencias de mi proyecto Android en <FIXTURE> y dime qué está desactualizado, agrupado por riesgo. De momento no cambies nada.
evals.expected_output: Same controlled flow as eval 1, with the whole user-facing response in Spanish.
assertions: Detected updates without editing the build (init script) or with the planner's metadata mode.
Flagged the latest core-ktx / Compose BOM as needing compileSdk 37 and offered compatible alternatives.
Listed AGP and the Gradle wrapper as separate items needing their own confirmation.
Flagged the old-scheme KSP as a prerequisite before any Kotlin bump.

User-facing response is in SPANISH, matching the prompt.
